clock.semantics: Integer day relative to admission. The article gives no calendar dates. day = null means the fact is valid at any point in the admission (the article gives no day). The treatment course is dated from the start of replacement, not from admission.

vignette: A 53-year-old woman with no significant past medical history presents to the emergency department with watery diarrhoea for 10 days and significant weight loss.
opening_statement_lay: I've had watery diarrhoea for about ten days now, and I've lost a lot of weight.

facts.release_text: Significant weight loss. Amount and period not recorded.
Liquid stools without blood or mucus.

facts.note: The article reports no haemorrhage on examination; the reviewer should confirm this may also be given as a history answer.

facts.release_text: No lymphadenopathy, hepatomegaly or splenomegaly (no tumour syndrome).

single_results.note: The article's 'normal range' of >120,000/mm3 is the usual threshold for a regenerative response, not a reference interval.
Reported as prothrombin activity in %, not seconds. The catalogue has no PT-activity component; linked to CMP.PT pending review.
The article prints 'mmol/L'; umol/L assumed. The catalogue has no unconjugated bilirubin component.
The catalogue has no numeric schistocyte component; also given to the Pathology Service in R01.
The article says these antibodies, with gastroscopy, 'confirmed' the diagnosis but gives no titre or method; positive is inferred.

raw_material.note: The article reports only the schistocyte count. Other film features are gap G07.

raw_material.findings: Marked hypercellularity with increased erythroblasts. Megaloblasts with fine chromatin and prominent nucleoli.
raw_material.note: The caption says H&E, which suggests a trephine or clot section rather than an aspirate smear; linked to the aspirate pending review.

raw_material.test: Upper GI endoscopy with gastric biopsies
raw_material.findings: Biopsies: atrophy of the fundic mucosa. Intestinal metaplasia.
raw_material.note: The article does not describe the endoscopic appearance. The catalogue has no separate gastric biopsy histology item; linked to the endoscopy.

final_dx.text: Pernicious anaemia (autoimmune atrophic gastritis) with severe vitamin B12 deficiency, presenting as pancytopenia with haemolysis and schistocytes that mimicked a thrombotic microangiopathy (pseudo-TMA)
accepted_synonyms: autoimmune atrophic gastritis with vitamin B12 deficiency

secondary_findings: IgG-positive direct antiglobulin test, which the authors discuss as possibly dysimmune and associated with pernicious anaemia; no autoimmune haemolytic anaemia treatment was needed
Prothrombin activity 44%, not explained in the article
Watery diarrhoea resolving with B12 replacement alone
accepted_differential: Haemolytic uraemic syndrome, including STEC-HUS given the diarrhoea
Warm autoimmune haemolytic anaemia or Evans syndrome (IgG-positive DAT)
Other causes of pancytopenia: marrow infiltration, aplastic anaemia, HIV
key_discriminators: normal renal function and no neurological impairment
PLASMIC score 4 (low risk of severe ADAMTS13 deficiency)
fundic atrophy with intestinal metaplasia on gastric biopsy
ground_truth.treatment_given: Vitamin B12 replacement (route, dose and schedule not reported). No plasma exchange.
ground_truth.outcome: Rapid improvement: diarrhoea resolved by day 4 and a reticulocyte response by day 7 of replacement, without other treatment. Follow-up values not reported.
must_do: Measure vitamin B12 and folate (before any transfusion) in macrocytic pancytopenia
Assess the pre-test probability of TTP (for example the PLASMIC score) and send ADAMTS13 if TTP remains possible
Recognise that a low reticulocyte count with haemolysis points to ineffective erythropoiesis
Find the cause: intrinsic factor and parietal cell antibodies, and gastroscopy with biopsies
Confirm the response: reticulocytes within about a week, then the blood count
must_not_do: Start plasma exchange for presumed TTP without weighing B12 deficiency and the PLASMIC score
Treat as autoimmune haemolytic anaemia with steroids on the IgG DAT alone
Give folic acid alone before B12 replacement

gaps.guidance: Article says 'stable haemodynamics'. Afebrile; heart rate mildly raised from anaemia; blood pressure normal; SpO2 normal.
Amount and period not reported. Reviewer sets a plausible figure (for example 6-8 kg over two to three months).
Soft, non-tender or mildly tender abdomen; no masses; no organomegaly (article: no tumour syndrome).
Article: no neurological impairment. Vibration sense, proprioception, reflexes and cognition normal. Do not invent posterior column signs.
Not reported. Reviewer decides: normal, or a smooth red tongue.
White cell count low-normal or low, consistent with neutrophils 1,050/mm3; lymphocytes normal; RDW raised; red cell count consistent with Hb 5.1 g/dL and MCV 113 fL.
Macro-ovalocytes, anisopoikilocytosis and hypersegmented neutrophils; polychromasia scanty; schistocytes as reported (2.3%); no blasts.
Article: renal function normal. Urea and creatinine within range; potassium normal or low-normal (diarrhoea).

gaps.item: Liver function (total and conjugated bilirubin, enzymes)
gaps.guidance: Total bilirubin raised, mostly unconjugated (free bilirubin 31 umol/L); AST mildly raised; ALT, ALP and GGT normal; albumin low-normal.
Consistent with prothrombin activity 44% (INR about 1.6-1.8). APTT normal or mildly prolonged; fibrinogen normal (no DIC).
Not reported. If ordered: not severely deficient (well above 10%). The catalogue has no ADAMTS13 item yet.
Folate normal; ferritin normal or raised; transferrin saturation normal or raised.
Not reported. Reviewer sets (positive supports the diagnosis; negative does not exclude it).
Not in the catalogue. If added: gastrin raised, pepsinogen I low, homocysteine and MMA raised.
Not described. Pale, thin fundic mucosa with visible vessels; antrum spared.
Culture, C. difficile toxin and ova and parasites negative.
No hepatosplenomegaly, mass or biliary dilatation.
Negative.

gaps.item: DAT C3d, eluate and antibody screen
gaps.guidance: C3d negative; antibody screen negative. Eluate reviewer-set.
TSH normal; anti-TPO reviewer-set (autoimmune thyroid disease often goes with this condition).
Mixed diet; no alcohol; no metformin, proton-pump inhibitor or nitrous oxide. General answers only, no diagnosis-specific negatives.
No known blood or autoimmune disease in the family, unless the reviewer decides otherwise.
Urobilinogen raised; no haemoglobinuria, proteinuria or haematuria.

gaps.item: Bone marrow details: iron stain, trephine, karyotype
gaps.guidance: Iron stores present, no ring sideroblasts; karyotype normal; no infiltrate.
Article: reticulocyte response by day 7 of replacement, no numbers. Reviewer sets values if a follow-up count is modelled.
